answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks through a slashable bond: every new identity must lock scarce capital before it can vote, transact, or build reputation. The protocol randomly assigns overlapping tasks to supposedly independent agents and slashes bonds when their answers reveal collusion or fabricated diversity. Honest identities recover their stake and gain influence, but an attacker must fund and risk a separate bond for every fake identity. Trust becomes an oasis on the terrace, while useful agents earn nectar.
